_what: A LABELLED must-fire/must-be-silent set for the recall matcher, over PLAN-STEP situations.
_why: Written and committed BEFORE running the matcher against it. Every earlier number in this build was derived from output I looked at first: the 17% fire rate came from 30 commands I chose, and the 'B3 looks promising' claim came from reading 195 matches and noticing the good ones. Reading a list and noticing hits cannot count MISSES, because a miss is invisible without a label. Committing the answers first is the only way this set can falsify anything.
_method: Situations are drawn from real `Doing:` lines written during this project's sessions, or are realistic paraphrases of moments that actually occurred. Expected entries were chosen by reading the memory corpus's triggers, NOT by running the matcher. Where more than one entry is genuinely right, `expect_any` lists them and surfacing any one counts as a hit.
_scoring: hit = the expected entry appears in the top N. miss = it does not. violation = a `must_be_silent` situation surfaces anything at all.
